security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel (S-mode) code or KVM assumes M-mode always has full access to S/U-mode memory, then calls into M-mode firmware (OpenSBI) via ECALL. Under Smepmp with MML=1 and MMAP=1, M-mode firmware is denied access to S/U-mode-only PMP regions, causing unexpected access-fault exceptions in firmware trap handlers that read/write S/U-mode pages (e.g., IPI, TLB shootdown, remote FENCE.I).
security_spec.summary: Smepmp MML=1 makes pmpcfg.L=0 regions S/U-mode-only (denied to M-mode); kernel SBI calls that pass S/U virtual addresses to M-mode firmware can fault if firmware hasn't mapped those addresses via M-mode-only or shared PMP regions
